description:
FILED s532e (Opus agent, 2026-11-03), found by the §48 list-slice probes (scratch/s532e/p/pre.pl).  PRE-EXISTING: main 4fb60297 and the s532e tree print the same.  A SILENT WRONG.

A list slice whose list holds a nested parenthesised group or an aggregate does not flatten it before indexing -- the slice indexes a list of sub-lists / references:

    my %hh = (a => 1); print "1 ", (%hh)[0], "\n";      # perl: 1 a        PCL: 1 a1
    print "2 ", ((1, 2), (3, 4))[2], "\n";              # perl: 2 3        PCL: 2 (empty)
    print "3 ", ((1, 2), 3)[1], "\n";                   # perl: 3 2        PCL: 3 3
    my @r = ((1, 2), 3)[0, 1]; print "5 @r\n";          # perl: 5 1 2      PCL: 5 ARRAY(0x1) 3
    my @s = (%hh)[0, 1]; print "6 @s\n";                # perl: 6 a 1      PCL: 6 HASH(0x2)

Controls that are right: `(1, 2, 3)[1]`, `(@a)[-1]`, `(@a, 7)[2]`, `(f())[0]`, `qw(a b c)[1, 2]`.  The list-slice node is an a_ref_acc marked list_ctx_subscript (Pl::PExpr arrow loop; ExprToCL gen_array_ref_access_form): its base must be the FLATTENED list in list context, as perl's lslice does (pp_lslice takes the list as pushed on the stack).

Also seen, probably a different mechanism: `print scalar(@{[ (1, 2, 3)[0, 1] ]})` -- perl 2, PCL 1 (while `my $t = [ (1, 2, 3)[0, 1] ]; scalar(@$t)` is 2).


=== DONE (s536f) ===
Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08.  FIXED (runtime only).  `%p-listslice-array` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) now flattens the literal list vector a list slice indexes whenever an element is not one slot (`%p-listslice-expands-p`: a nested list / an array / a hash / the %ENV marker / a built-in's NIL) -- `%p-listslice-flatten` spreads each element by the ARGUMENT walk's rule (an array via `%p-flatten-vector-into`, a hash via the new shared `%p-flatten-hash-into`, which `%p-flatten-arg-into` now calls too), so an element is its slot's cell; NIL contributes nothing.  The real-array hot path (`$aref->[i]`) returns before any other test.  Also: a VECTOR index to `p-aref-deref-box` (a list slice in an lvalue slot, `[ (1,2,3)[0,1] ]`) is the slice -- it read ONE element (the task's "different mechanism", the same site).  Probes scratch/s536f/p/m1.pl m1g.pl m1i.pl: every row of the reproducer = perl; FIXED beside it `((sort ...), 9)[1,3]` and `(%h, (@a))[2,3]`, `(lstat $missing, 1)[0]`.  Guard Pl/t/list-slice-01.t row 21 (FAILS on c8886b61).  Residue filed: #4682 (a list slice in an ALIASING consumer copies), #4683 (`f(%$blessed)` passes the object).
